hate.en: Ooh, when I was little, I used to absolutely hate nuts and avocados.
hate.zh: 哦，我小时候绝对讨厌坚果和牛油果。

hate.en: But you, I would sit there and be like, wow, you really hate me.
hate.zh: 但我会坐在那儿想，哇，你真的恨我。

hate.en: At medical school in Edinburgh, he quickly discovered that he hated the sight of surgery.
hate.zh: 在爱丁堡的医学院里，他很快发现自己极其讨厌看到手术的血腥场面。

hate.en: Hmm. I'm going to say deep cleaning the oven because I really hate that job.
hate.zh: 嗯。我猜是深度清洁烤箱，因为我真的很讨厌那项工作。

hate.en: I had to scratch loads and loads. Oh, I hate it when that happens.
hate.zh: 我不得不使劲地挠个不停。哦，我最讨厌这种情况了。

harm.en: Conservation is the protection of plants, animals and the natural world from human harm.
harm.zh: 保护（Conservation）是指保护植物、动物和自然世界免受人类伤害。

harm.en: And there was the physical and psychological distance from the person being harmed.
harm.zh: 此外，还有与受害者之间物理上和心理上的距离感。

harm.en: Maslach told him that the experiment was unethical and that the prisoners were suffering real harm.
harm.zh: Maslach 告诉他，这场实验不道德，囚犯们正在遭受真实的伤害。

harm.en: Critics pointed out that Musk’s access to federal systems could benefit his companies while harming competitors.
harm.zh: 批评人士指出，Musk 访问联邦系统的权限可能会使他的公司受益，同时损害竞争对手的利益。

harm.en: And it can no longer damage the skin and harm ourselves.
harm.zh: 这样它们就无法再损伤皮肤、伤害我们自己了。

harmful.en: If something harmful is left unchecked, nobody controls it or prevents it from growing.
harmful.zh: 如果某种有害的东西被 left unchecked(放任不管)，就是说没有人控制它或阻止它继续扩大。

harmful.en: But now all the YouTube doctor experts are telling us seed oils are harmful.
harmful.zh: 但现在所有的油管医生专家都在告诉我们，种子油是有害的。

harmful.en: Modern ethical guidelines for psychological experiments would see it as far too harmful.
harmful.zh: 按照现代心理学实验的伦理准则，这场实验的危害性实在太大了。

harmful.en: So, Neil, itching is our skin's way of protecting itself against harmful parasites.
harmful.zh: 所以，Neil，痒其实是皮肤用来抵御有害寄生虫的一种自我保护方式。

harmful.en: Tracking behavior in apps or on websites does not necessarily prevent harmful behavior in digital spaces.
harmful.zh: 在应用程序中或网站上追踪行为并不一定能防止数字空间中的有害行为。

hardly.en: So, to wrap things up, today, we hardly need to think about leap years.
hardly.zh: 所以，总而言之，今天我们几乎不需要考虑闰年。

hardly.en: And this was hardly a difficult question to answer: list five things they did that week.
hardly.zh: 而且这几乎不是一个难回答的问题：列出他们那周做的五项工作。

hardly.en: It's hardly surprising people called him “the wolf of the Indian Ocean”.
hardly.zh: 难怪人们称他为“印度洋之狼”。

hardly.en: In many ways, it was hardly surprising. There were question marks over what to do with nuclear waste.
hardly.zh: 从很多方面来看，这并不令人意外。如何处理核废料一直存在疑问。

hardly.en: So it’s hardly surprising that this, that speaking, this is the skill that so many companies are focusing on.
hardly.zh: 因此，毫不奇怪，这是口语，这是许多公司都在关注的技能。

habit.en: So, Georgie, how can parents help their children develop good eating habits?
habit.zh: 那么，乔治，父母如何帮助他们的孩子养成良好的饮食习惯呢？

habit.en: Once he broke that habit, he just applied it to writing and building TV shows.
habit.zh: 一旦他戒掉了那个习惯，他就把它应用到了写作和制作电视节目上。

habit.en: The habit of code switching when things get difficult slows down the development of your automatic fluency.
habit.zh: 当事情变难时就进行语码转换的习惯会减慢你自动流利度的发展。

habit.en: But as she started to focus ever more intensely on work, she slipped back into some old habits.
habit.zh: 但随着她越来越专注于工作，她又滑回了一些旧习惯。

habit.en: But it can become a problem. It becomes a problem when code switching turns into an unconscious habit.
habit.zh: 但它可能会变成一个问题。当语码转换变成一种无意识的习惯时，它就成了问题。

handy.en: Like, I stocked up on things all at once whether than keeping it handy just in case.
handy.zh: 就像是一次性把东西囤够，而不是以防万一随用随买。

handy.en: Hmm. Finally, my English degree might come in handy!
handy.zh: 嗯。终于，我的英语学位派上用场了！

handle.en: The biggest of these is privacy. One major concern is how personal data is handled.
handle.zh: 其中最大的一个是隐私。一个主要的担忧是个人数据如何被处理。

handle.en: If you can't handle something, you find it difficult to deal or cope with.
handle.zh: 如果你无法应对（can't handle）某事，你会发现很难处理或应付它。

handle.en: When Chhavi returned to India after living overseas, she says she couldn't handle the noise.
handle.zh: 当Chhavi在海外生活后回到印度时，她说她无法忍受这种噪音。

handle.en: By spring, the panic had grown so big that the local magistrates couldn’t handle it anymore.
handle.zh: 到了春天，恐慌情绪扩散得如此之大，以至于当地治安官再也无法控制局面了。

handle.en: I know who he is. I can handle being in a space named for John C.
handle.zh: 我知道他是谁。我可以接受生活在一个以约翰·C·

harden.en: Mathilde's spice shop holds pepper tasting sessions, where she explains to customers the origin of her peppers and how they grow, changing colour as they harden in the sun.
harden.zh: Mathilde 的香料店会举办胡椒品鉴会，她会向顾客解释胡椒的来源和生长方式，以及它们在阳光下变硬时是如何变色的。

harvest.en: So, for a while, you're trying to harvest whales more and more effectively.
harvest.zh: 所以，有一段时间，你一直在想办法更高效地捕鲸。

harvest.en: A food's maturity refers to the stage when it's fully grown and ready for harvest.
harvest.zh: 食物的 maturity（成熟度）指的是它完全长大并准备好收获的阶段。

harvest.en: A food's maturity describes the stage when a food is fully grown and ready to harvest.
harvest.zh: 食物的 maturity（成熟度）描述的是食物完全长大并准备好收获的阶段。

harvest.en: So now we have the same person, a month before harvest, poor, and a month after harvest, well-off.
harvest.zh: 所以现在我们有了同一个人，收获前一个月很穷，收获后一个月很富裕。

harvest.en: So now we have the same person, a month before harvest, poor, and a month after harvest, well-off.
harvest.zh: 所以现在我们有了同一个人，收获前一个月很穷，收获后一个月很富裕。

hang.en: "What?", he asks, before declaring that the boy will be hanged one day.
hang.zh: “什么？”他问道，接着断言这个男孩有一天会被绞死。

hang.en: What Silvia really looks forward to is chillin' – a slang word meaning relaxing or hanging out.
hang.zh: Silvia 真正期待的是“chillin'”——这是一个俚语，意思是放松或闲逛。

hang.en: There were the Hanging Gardens of Babylon, which may or may not have actually existed.
hang.zh: 还有巴比伦空中花园，它到底存不存在可能还要打个问号。

hang.en: Hang on. What if this is a sign that I'm not supposed to be here?
hang.zh: 等等。如果这预示着我不该待在这里怎么办？

hang.en: Many were humiliated before being sentenced to death by hanging, strangled slowly with piano wire.
hang.zh: 许多人在被判处绞刑前受到羞辱，用钢琴线被缓慢勒死。

hawk.en: Was it: a) Stephen Hawking, b) Albert Einstein, or c) Marie Curie?
hawk.zh: 是：a) Stephen Hawking，b) Albert Einstein，还是 c) Marie Curie？

hawk.en: Was it a) Stephen Hawking, b) Albert Einstein, or c) Marie Curie?
hawk.zh: 是 a) Stephen Hawking，b) Albert Einstein，还是 c) Marie Curie？

hammer.en: People from Berlin used hammers and chisels to break pieces from the wall.
hammer.zh: 柏林人用锤子和凿子砸下墙上的碎片。

hammer.en: Is it a) the hammer, b) the anvil, or c) the stirrup bone?
hammer.zh: 是 a) 锤骨，b) 砧骨，还是 c) 镫骨？

hammer.en: And then that's passed on to the three smallest bones in the body: the hammer, the anvil and the stirrup.
hammer.zh: 接着，声音被传递到人体内最小的三块骨头：锤骨、砧骨和镫骨。

hammer.en: There's another real hammer blow. You don't get very touchy-feely with like, you know, I live in Austin now, so I'm like in the psychedelic mecca of the United States.
hammer.zh: 这是另一个真正的重击。你不会变得非常感性，你知道，我现在住在奥斯汀，所以我身处美国的迷幻麦加。

hammer.en: This is not a question of whether there would be thousands of astronauts with hammers and shovels physically digging the surface themselves, and lugging large sacks back at the end of the day, but rather whether the mine would be 100% automated, controlled from back on Earth or from a space mission closer to Earth, or whether there would be human astronauts monitoring the situation from the site, just in case anything went wrong.
hammer.zh: 这并不是说会有成千上万的宇航员拿着锤子和铁锹亲自在表面挖掘，最后背着大麻袋回来，而是说这个矿场会是 100% 自动化的，由地球后方或距离地球更近的太空任务进行控制，亦或是会有宇航员在现场监控情况以防万一出现任何差错。

halve.en: She halves her page: pros, cons. And she said by the end of it, she knows what she's doing.
halve.zh: 她把纸对折：利，弊。她说做完之后，她就知道该怎么做了。

halve.en: But Ole claims his technique halves the amount of water needed to grow fruit trees, and that most farmers will make back their investment within two years.
halve.zh: 但奥莱声称，他的技术将种植果树所需的水量减半，并且大多数农民能在两年内收回投资。

ham.en: In many cases we say, " Che song ham ni da." This is used in formal situations or with people we don't know well, and we often bow when saying, " Che song ham ni da."
ham.zh: 在许多情况下，我们会说“Che song ham ni da”。这用于正式场合或我们不太熟悉的人，我们在说“Che song ham ni da”时经常会鞠躬。

ham.en: In many cases we say, " Che song ham ni da." This is used in formal situations or with people we don't know well, and we often bow when saying, " Che song ham ni da."
ham.zh: 在许多情况下，我们会说“Che song ham ni da”。这用于正式场合或我们不太熟悉的人，我们在说“Che song ham ni da”时经常会鞠躬。

hateful.en: Andrea says the more reaction a post gets, the more money the creator makes, even if the reactions are hateful.
hateful.zh: 安德里亚表示，一条帖子获得的反应越多，创作者赚的钱就越多，即使这些反应是充满仇恨的。

hateful.en: Don't. And I think that has been one of the things that has diffused so many of these like hateful comments where people dehumanize you or whatever and make you into this ideal that they reject.
hateful.zh: 别过。我认为这已经成为化解许多这种仇恨评论的事情之一，人们将你非人化，或者把你变成他们所拒绝的某种理想。

hamburger.en: For example, the shalpuborgari, or shop burger, was a take on – or variation of – the American hamburger.
hamburger.zh: 例如，shalpuborgari，或者叫店锯汉堡，就是对美式汉堡的一种改编或变种。

hamburger.en: In the United States, cheap and easy food like hamburgers, French fries and milkshakes have been popular since the 1950s.
hamburger.zh: 在美嚽，像汉堡、薯条和啡啡泡茶这类便宜又简便的食物自 20 世纪 50 年代以来就一直很受欢迎。

harmonious.en: It seems Vera, Nuala and Eileen have remained close friends as they've grown up, but the relationship between older, middle and younger sisters isn’t always so harmonious.
harmonious.zh: 看来维拉、努拉和艾琳在长大的过程中一直保持着亲密的友情，但大姐、二姐和妹妹之间的关系并不总是那么和谐。

hall.en: Was it: a) Hyde Park? b) The Royal Albert Hall? or c) Finsbury Park?
hall.zh: 是：a) 海德公园？b) 皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅？还是 c) 芬斯伯里公园？

hall.en: It is the winter of 1837. A small boy stands in a large stone hall.
hall.zh: 那是 1837 年的冬天。一个瘦小的男孩站在宽大的石头大厅里。

hall.en: The anthropologist Edward T. Hall introduced another useful way of distinguishing between cultures.
hall.zh: 人类学家爱德华·T·霍尔（Edward T. Hall）提出了另一种区分文化的有用方法。

hall.en: We've arrived at Act Two of our program, Act Two, Kids in the Hall.
hall.zh: 我们来到了节目的第二幕，第二幕是“礼拜堂里的小孩”。

hall.en: Yeah, you know, when I was a kid, there was a rumor in the Hall.
hall.zh: 对，你知道的，当我还是个孩子的时候，聚会所里流传着一个传言。

haunt.en: And there's also the question that has haunted nuclear power for seventy years: nuclear waste.
haunt.zh: 此外，还有一个困扰了核能70年的问题：核废料。

haunt.en: Some told him that the experience still haunted them.
haunt.zh: 有些人告诉他，这段经历至今仍萦绕在心头，挥之不去。

haunt.en: Instead, the war raged on, and the failed coup of July 20th went down as one of history’s most haunting ‘what ifs’.
haunt.zh: 然而，战火仍在继续，7月20日的未遂政变作为历史上最令人挥之不去的“如果”之一载入了史册。

haunt.en: During those long, haunted nights on the Western Front, his mind drifted back to the lush green canopy of South America, to the gentle currents of unknown rivers, and to the stories of that hidden city.
haunt.zh: 在西线战场那些漫长而挥之不去的夜晚里，他的思绪飘回了南美洲郁郁葱葱的绿色树冠、不知名河流的柔和水流，以及关于那座隐藏城市的种种传说。

harsh.en: While indigenous people and enslaved Africans usually lived in poverty and faced harsh discrimination.
harsh.zh: 而土著人民和被奴役的非洲人通常生活在贫困之中，并面临着严重的歧视。

harsh.en: This name reflected their low status and harsh working conditions, and I think originated from Singapore.
harsh.zh: 这个名字反映了他们低下的社会地位和恶劣的工作条件，我想它起源于新加坡。

harsh.en: After all, the winter had been harsh, and disease wasn’t uncommon.
harsh.zh: 毕竟冬天很严酷，生病并不罕见。

harsh.en: In it, he describes the harsh day-to-day lives of the working class in the North of England.
harsh.zh: 在书中，他描绘了英格兰北部工人阶级严酷的日常生活。

harsh.en: But instead, the opposite happened. The guards became even harsher.
harsh.zh: 但恰恰相反，情况变得更糟。狱警变得更加严厉。

harbour.en: The explorers had entered Guanabara Bay, the large natural harbour but not a river.
harbour.zh: 探险家们进入的是瓜纳巴拉湾这个巨大的天然港口，而不是一条河。

harbour.en: And Rio’s harbour made it one of the best ports in the entire Atlantic.
harbour.zh: 而且里约的港口使其成为整个大西洋最好的港口之一。

harbour.en: Lawrence, the British archaeologist and army officer who fought alongside Arabian tribesmen for a united Arab nation, all while harbouring a guilty secret.
harbour.zh: Lawrence，这位英国考古学家兼军官曾与阿拉伯部落并肩作战，为建立一个统一的阿拉伯国家而奋斗，同时内心还隐藏着一个令他愧疚的秘密。

harbour.en: Its navy dominated the western Mediterranean, its harbours were filled with goods from across North Africa, southern Spain, Sicily, even as far as the British Isles.
harbour.zh: 它的海军称霸西地中海，港口里停满了来自北非、西班牙南部、西西里岛，甚至远至不列颠群岛的货物。

harbour.en: They had pulled down the statue of Edward Colston, an eighteenth-century slave trader, during the Black Lives Matter protests of June 2020, and they had thrown the statue into Bristol harbour.
harbour.zh: 在2020年6月"黑人的命也是命"(Black Lives Matter)抗议活动期间，他们推倒了十八世纪奴隶贩子爱德华·科尔斯顿(Edward Colston)的雕像，并把雕像扔进了布里斯托尔港。

hatred.en: He said, hatred isn't something you avoid.
hatred.zh: 他说：仇恨不是你需要避免的东西。

hatred.en: He said that " desecration is awful" and that his government was " committed to tackling all forms of hatred and division."
hatred.zh: 他表示“亵渎是可怕的”，并且他的政府“致力于打击一切形式的仇恨和分裂”。

hatred.en: Well, it's just, it's hard to think that the people you used to have contempt for, or distaste or hatred or whatever shaped you in a way that you couldn't have been.
hatred.zh: 嗯，只是，很难想象那些你曾经鄙视、厌恶或憎恨的人，竟然以一种你无法想象的方式塑造了你。

hatred.en: The boy’s name was Hannibal. Now, to understand why a father might make his child swear eternal hatred towards another state, we need to look at the world Hannibal was born into.
hatred.zh: 这个男孩名叫Hannibal。现在，为了理解为什么一个父亲会要求自己的孩子发誓对另一个国家永世为敌，我们需要看看Hannibal出生的那个世界。

hatred.en: Almost immediately, he recognised the voice, the intense, almost obsessive way of arguing, the deep-seated hatred of technology, even certain specific and unusual expressions and turns of phrase that he knew his brother used.
hatred.zh: 几乎立刻，他就认出了那个声音、那种强烈且几乎带有强迫症的辩论方式、对科技根深蒂固的仇恨，甚至还有他知道他哥哥用过的一些特定且不寻常的表达和措辞。

halt.en: In a halting, tearful voice, he delivered a prepared statement confessing to his alleged crimes and begging the North Korean government for forgiveness.
halt.zh: 他用断断续续、带着哭腔的声音，宣读了一份事先准备好的声明，承认了他被指控的罪行，并恳求朝鲜政府的原谅。

haircut.en: A funny hermit kingdom ruled by a despot with an unconventional haircut.
haircut.zh: 它不只是一个由一个留着奇特发型的独裁者统治的、有点滑稽的隐士王国。

haircut.en: You know? Hey man, that hurts. I know you think my haircut looked funny, but the way you said it in front of those other people, it hurts.
haircut.zh: 上一次男性朋友看着另一个男性朋友说‘你伤害了我’是什么时候？

hazardous.en: His ten-year journey back home is equally hazardous, and he has to evade cyclopes, giants, sorceresses, and various gods who mean him harm.
hazardous.zh: 他历时十年的回乡之旅同样危机重重，他不得不躲避独眼巨人、巨人、女巫以及各种心怀恶意的神灵。

hail.en: Project Hail Mary is an extreme example, but there are much clearer examples.
hail.zh: 《挽救计划》是一个极端的例子，但现实中有更明显的例子。

hail.en: And, sure enough, he arrived in Rome and was hailed as emperor.
hail.zh: 果然，他抵达罗马并被欢呼为皇帝。

hail.en: I just finished listening to the audiobook of the novel “Project Hail Mary” by Andy Weir, which has recently become a very successful Hollywood movie.
hail.zh: 我刚刚听完了安迪·威尔（Andy Weir）的小说《挽救计划》（Project Hail Mary）的有声书，这部作品最近改编成了好莱坞大热电影。

hatch.en: In the hit political drama, House of Cards, the Machiavellian protagonist, Frank Underwood, hatches a plot to become President.
hatch.zh: 在热门政治剧《纸牌屋》中，善于权谋的主角弗兰克·安德伍德密谋成为总统。

hatch.en: Neither leader was keen on the idea of combining forces, but unbeknownst to them, there was another plan being hatched.
hatch.zh: 两位领袖都不太热衷于合并的想法，但他们不知道的是，另一个计划正在酝酿之中。

hatch.en: Next up, in part two, will be an episode on Simon Mann, the ex-Etonian who tried to hatch a plot to launch a coup in Equatorial Guinea.
hatch.zh: 接下来，在第二部分中，将有一集关于 Simon Mann 的节目，这位前伊顿公学学生曾企图在赤道几内亚发动政变。

hassle.en: He was frequently hassled and shaken down for bribes, forced to pay money to the police.
hassle.zh: 他经常受到骚扰和勒索敲诈，被迫向警察交钱。

hassle.en: There are problems. Individual mortgages are too big a hassle for the global pool of money.
hassle.zh: 这里有问题。对全球资金池来说，单笔抵押贷款太麻烦了。

hassle.en: So what Mike and his peers on Wall Street did, was to figure out a way to give the global pool of money all the benefits of a mortgage-- basically higher yield-- without all the hassle and risk.
hassle.zh: 因此，Mike 和他在华尔街的同僚们所做的，就是想出一个办法，把抵押贷款的所有好处——基本上是更高收益——在没有所有麻烦和风险的情况下打包给全球资金池。

handful.en: Initially, it was a poor, religious order, with no real financial resources and just a handful of knights.
handful.zh: 最初，这是一个贫穷的宗教修会，没有真正的财政资源，只有区区几个骑士。

handful.en: John Booy is a close friend of Betsy DeVos, one of a handful of people she brought to her confirmation hearing.
handful.zh: John Booy是Betsy DeVos的密友，也是她带去参加确认听证会的少数几个人之一。

handful.en: But not everyone agrees. The symptoms don’t match perfectly, nor does the timeline, and ergot poisoning would’ve hit more people, not just a handful of girls.
handful.zh: 但并非所有人都赞同这种说法。症状并不完全吻合，时间线也对不上，而且如果真是麦角菌中毒，受害者应该更多，而不仅仅是少数几个女孩。

handful.en: One of the most interesting conversations I had. but I was I analyzed people like you know there's a handful of podcasts are really great there's a couple million in the directory only a handful are really great yours is really great and I'm like why the hell how it's unfair this guy is like gifted at music and now he's gifted podcasting why is this the case and what I came up with and I started analyzing and thinking about what you do in your day job what you've done for over four decades and I was like he's a professional listener That's true.
handful.zh: 那是我进行过最有趣的对话之一。但我分析过像你这样的人，你知道，播客里有几百万个节目，但真正出色的只有寥寥几个，你的节目真的很棒。我就在想，凭什么？这不公平，这家伙在音乐上天赋异禀，现在做播客也这么有天赋，这是为什么？我分析并思考了你几十年来一直从事的主业，我意识到，你是一个专业的倾听者。确实如此。

handful.en: One of the most interesting conversations I had. but I was I analyzed people like you know there's a handful of podcasts are really great there's a couple million in the directory only a handful are really great yours is really great and I'm like why the hell how it's unfair this guy is like gifted at music and now he's gifted podcasting why is this the case and what I came up with and I started analyzing and thinking about what you do in your day job what you've done for over four decades and I was like he's a professional listener That's true.
handful.zh: 那是我进行过最有趣的对话之一。但我分析过像你这样的人，你知道，播客里有几百万个节目，但真正出色的只有寥寥几个，你的节目真的很棒。我就在想，凭什么？这不公平，这家伙在音乐上天赋异禀，现在做播客也这么有天赋，这是为什么？我分析并思考了你几十年来一直从事的主业，我意识到，你是一个专业的倾听者。确实如此。

harmony.en: Sometimes, it seems that the natural world has been created in complete harmony with mathematic principles.
harmony.zh: 有时候，自然界似乎完全遵循数学原理创造出来。

harmony.en: Perhaps, he mused, the true measure of civilisation wasn’t bombs and factories, and industrial output, but wisdom and harmony—qualities that might lie undiscovered beneath the rainforest’s thick foliage.
harmony.zh: 他沉思着，或许文明真正的标尺不是炸弹、工厂和工业产出，而是智慧与和谐——这些品质或许正静静地躺在雨林厚重枝叶下，等待着被发掘。

haul.en: Still, there are some commentators who have pointed out that, even with a relatively small haul of precious metals, asteroid mining could be very detrimental to lower-income countries that have so-far relied on natural resource extraction.
haul.zh: 尽管如此，一些评论员指出，即使带着相对较少量的贵金属，小行星采矿也可能对迄今为止一直依赖自然资源开采的低收入国家造成极大损害。

handsome.en: She called the police, and several days later the tall, handsome man was tracked down and stopped by the police.
handsome.zh: 她报了警，几天后，那名高大英俊的男子被警方追踪并拦截。

handsome.en: Police around the world were told to keep a look out for a tall, handsome British man with a smooth, polished accent.
handsome.zh: 全球警察都接到通知，要留意一名身材高大、长相英俊、操着一口流利考究口音的英国男子。

handwriting.en: But the Japanese Language Proficiency Test does not require handwriting.
handwriting.zh: 但是日语能力测试并不要求手写。

handwriting.en: I did write, I did learn how to write the Japanese characters, some of them, but I just didn’t really practice writing, handwriting especially.
handwriting.zh: 我确实写过，我也学过怎么写日语汉字，其中的一部分，但我真的没有练习写作，尤其是手写。

harbor.en: There was the Colossus of Rhodes, which was a giant bronze statue that stood near a harbor in Greece.
harbor.zh: 还有罗德岛太阳神巨像，那是矗立在希腊港口附近的巨大青铜雕像。

harbor.en: A group of colonists boarded a British ship in Boston Harbor and dumped hundreds of chests of tea into the water.
harbor.zh: 一群殖民地居民登上波士顿港的一艘英国船只，把数百箱茶倒进了水里。

hardship.en: In times of economic hardship or political repression, frustration builds slowly.
hardship.zh: 在经济困难或政治高压时期，挫折感慢慢积聚。

hardship.en: In countries without strong or universal healthcare, like the USA, medical costs are one of the leading causes of financial hardship.
hardship.zh: 在没有健全或全民医保的国家（如美国），医疗费用是导致经济困难的主要原因之一。

hardy.en: In fact, Hardy once said that his greatest contribution to mathematics was discovering Ramanujan.
hardy.zh: 事实上，Hardy曾说过，他对数学最大的贡献就是发现了Ramanujan。

hardy.en: When Ramanujan and Hardy finally met, it was the meeting of two completely different worlds.
hardy.zh: 当Ramanujan和Hardy终于见面时，这是两个截然不同的世界的碰撞。

hamper.en: Because, the temptations of rent-seeking to hamper innovators is so depressing and so important for understanding why certain countries stay poor.
hamper.zh: 因为，寻租行为对创新者的阻挠诱惑实在令人沮丧，而这对于理解为什么某些国家始终贫穷又至关重要。

hamper.en: But there's this last piece, and we'll close with this, which comes from a paper of William Baumol and rent-seeking, and how we should think about the wealth of nations, and where is it productive to spend your time in creating new products that help people or in creating new regulations that hamper your competitors?
hamper.zh: 但还有最后一块拼图，我们就以此作结——它来自威廉·鲍莫尔关于寻租的一篇论文，涉及我们该如何看待国民财富，以及把时间花在创造能帮助人们的新产品上、还是花在制定阻碍竞争对手的新规上，哪个才更具生产性？

harp.en: I'm sorry to keep harping on evolution, but within biology, there's very few good explanatory theories and, you know, theory of evolution by natural selection is probably the best one.
harp.zh: 很抱歉一直谈论进化论，但在生物学中，很少有好的解释理论，你知道，自然选择的进化论可能是最好的一个。

hardware.en: On Tesla versus Waymo, would you bet on software or hardware for self-driving?
hardware.zh: 关于Tesla对比Waymo，你会押注软件还是硬件进行自动驾驶？

hay.en: My dad made me go shovel hay for a summer.
hay.zh: 我爸爸让我去铲了一个夏天的干草。

hazard.en: These people have literally been with me on a journey where they've got their own lives. but our journeys have been intertwined because they always make me want to be more and do more and grow more and change it and I think I do the same thing for them and we're constantly challenging each other and and encouraging each other and playing with each other and and and that that has been I mean that's been immeasurable for me you know that that's I even value that more than I do like let's say success on the subject of success friendship sacrifice the moment when you come to the united states um you are very hard working to say the least in fact when we sat down you know you've flown from portugal to where was it seattle seattle to vegas yeah then here to new york right in the last couple of days or so yeah it's four days i think in tot yeah yeah four days you don't have to do that you don't have to do that i mean you don't i mean i don't know what's in your bank account but i would hazard a guess that you don't need the money so i often wonder what is it that's driving you today someone said to me the day on the podcast they said they referred to my driving force in my life as potentially being toxic fuel and i've never had the phrase toxic fuel before but the definition of that is this sort of combination of seemingly negative forces that pushes you to to prove something whether it's to yourself or to others or okay and shame is a big part of that i mean you see it a lot i think with first-generation immigrants when they come to a country.
hazard.zh: 这些人确实陪我走过了一段旅程，他们有自己的生活，但我们的旅程交织在一起，因为他们总是让我想要变得更多、做得更多、成长更多、改变更多。我想我也为他们做了同样的事，我们不断地挑战彼此、鼓励彼此、一起玩耍。那对我来说是不可估量的，你知道，我甚至比所谓的成功更看重这一点。说到成功、友谊和牺牲，当你来到美国时，嗯，你非常努力工作，至少可以这么说。事实上，当我们坐下来时，你知道，你从葡萄牙飞到哪里？西雅图？西雅图到拉斯维加斯，是的，然后到纽约，对吧？在过去几天左右。是的，我想总共四天。是的，四天。你没必要这样做，你没必要这样做。我是说，我不知道你的银行账户里有多少钱，但我敢猜你并不缺钱。所以我经常想，到底是什么在驱动你今天前进？有人在播客上对我说，他们把我的生活动力称为潜在的“有毒燃料”，我以前从未听过“有毒燃料”这个词，但它的定义是：这种看似负面的力量组合，推动你去证明某些事情，无论是对自己还是对他人。羞耻感是其中的很大一部分。我的意思是，我认为第一代移民来到一个国家时，你会经常看到这种情况。
